memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"The Israelites said to them, 'If only we had died by the LORD's hand in Egypt!
There we sat around pots of meat and ate all the food we wanted, but you have
brought us out into this desert to starve this entire assembly to death.'"
- Ex 16:3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"There we sat around pots of meat and ate all the food we wanted."

Is that true? Not remotely. They were slaves. Exodus 1 describes ruthless
labour, bitter lives, and murdered infants. Exodus 2 says they groaned and cried
out. Nobody sits comfortably around pots of meat while their babies are being
drowned.

Hunger has rewritten history. That is what this verse is really about.

We do the same. When the present is painful, the past starts to glow. The
drinker remembers the ease and forgets the shame. The person who left a
destructive relationship remembers being wanted and forgets being crushed. The
memory becomes selective, and the selection is never accidental. It always
edits out precisely the reasons we left.

This is why remembering rightly matters so much, and why God kept telling them
to observe the Passover. Honest memory is a defence against this pull.

Notice also the accusation: "you have brought us out into this desert to
starve." They attribute cruel intent to God's rescue. Fear does not only distort
the past; it slanders the present.

If the old life is starting to look good, stop and ask honestly what you have
edited out.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What are you remembering more fondly than it deserves?
2. What did you actually leave behind, honestly told?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, when hunger or hardship makes my old life look better than it was, give
me honest memory. Keep me from slandering Your goodness. Amen.
